commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Omit absent fields from /inference/v1/generate stream chunks
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #53187. Python `/inference/v1/generate` stream chunks serialized absent optional fields as `null`, except for the two prompt-metadata keys that #53187 excluded per-field. The Rust frontend omits every absent field (`skip_serializing_none`), and the Python final usage chunk already uses `exclude_none=True`.

Serialize all Python data chunks with `exclude_none=True` so:

- both frontends emit identical stream JSON (absent `usage`, `logprobs`, `finish_reason`, `prompt_token_ids`, `mm_placeholders` are omitted, not `null`);
- the per-field `exclude` special case from #53187 goes away;
- Python data chunks and the final usage chunk follow the same rule.

Non-streaming responses are unchanged on both sides. Clients that read `chunk["finish_reason"]` on non-final Python chunks must use `.get()`; the OpenAI-style clients and prime-rl's generate client already do.

### Why this is not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `exclude_none`, `skip_serializing_none`, `generate stream` and `token_in_token_out`. #47933 changes abort `finish_reason` on this path but not serialization; no overlap. Independent of #57265 (empty-chunk skip rule).

## Test Plan

- Python: new `test_stream_chunks_omit_absent_fields`; existing key-absence assertions for the metadata fields unchanged.
- Rust: new `stream_chunk_omits_absent_fields` unit test locking the existing `skip_serializing_none` contract.

## Test Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py -q
# 33 passed

# 413 passed
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-server --tests --no-default-features -- -D warnings
# clean; cargo fmt --check clean
```

Model evaluation is not applicable: wire-format-only change, generated tokens are unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][Multimodal] Add cross-encoder caching to Mooncake P2P
commits.pr_body:
## Motivation and design

When an image reaches an Encoder that lacks its output locally, a shared Store
can reuse an embedding already computed by another Encoder. This change adds
cross-Encoder output reuse in normal EPD serving, with Mooncake Store as the
cache backend and the existing `ECMooncakeConnector` for P2P delivery. Normal
serving requests populate the Store as they compute outputs.

The Store resolves content identifiers against Encoder-derived tensor contracts
before encoding. Hits skip the Encoder; misses retain normal computation. Both
sources enter the local cache; serving requests then use the configured EC
transport. Store policy accepts tensors and output contracts, without P2P
reservations or destinations.
Only the Mooncake integration is enabled in this PR.

Serving requests arrive with their Prefill destination already selected.

```text
                      Encoder scheduler
                local miss → normal allocation
                              │
                              ▼
               Encoder worker: Store lookup/load
                  (shared Mooncake Store, RAM)
                              │
                ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
                ▼                           ▼
            Store hit              Miss / recoverable failure
         reuse embedding              Encoder forward
                │                           ├── async PUT → shared Store
                └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                              ▼
                  Local Encoder output cache
                              │
                              ▼
                   Configured EC transport
                              │
                              ▼
                           Prefill
```

Current serving integration: `Configured EC transport = ECMooncakeConnector P2P`.
Store resolution and publication are invoked by the Mooncake Encoder worker.

PUT lazily registers one reusable CPU header per client; payload registration
remains per embedding. The publisher drains before header unregistration.

Publication is bounded, asynchronous and best-effort; request completion does
not acknowledge Store readiness. Concurrent cold requests may still duplicate
computation. Hits are read with native `batch_get_into` through one reusable
registered buffer, pinned for CUDA outputs. The synchronous resolver chunks
reads by byte capacity, validates full objects and copies into independent
tensors before reusing staging. A rejected registration unwinds before falling
back. Batch GET rejections with `INVALID_PARAMS` (-600), `INVALID_REPLICA`
(-702), and completed GETs with
`LEASE_EXPIRED` (-707) fall back to encoding; a PUT rejected for
`TENANT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (-1700) skips publication. Unconfirmed native I/O or
unregistration retains buffer owners and fails explicitly.

## Usage

Set `cross_encoder_cache: true` in the producer's `ec_connector_extra_config`
and configure a RAM Store through `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`. Initial support is
images, MRv2, Encoder TP1, contiguous 2D FP16/BF16/FP32 outputs and no dynamic LoRA.
Shared reuse requires `--mm-processor-cache-gb` greater than zero to preserve
content identifiers; the processor-cache-off combination is rejected at startup.
`store_read_buffer_bytes` controls read staging separately from the publication
budget (default 128 MiB). It is allocated on the first Store hit; full misses
allocate none. Objects larger than the buffer fall back to encoding.
Prefill keeps its P2P configuration. EC and KV share Store configuration/setup.
`embedding_model_identity` overrides only the Store key's model field; matching
vLLM multimodal identifiers are still required, so this override alone does not
enable reuse across different configured model paths.
See `docs/features/cross_encoder_cache.md` for configuration and failure semantics.

## Validation

Self-contained CPU tests, with native Store I/O faked:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/ec_connector/unit -q \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_cross_encoder_cache.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_worker_ec_connector.py
```

51 cases passed (45 focused Store cases and 6 existing wrapper cases), covering
MRv2 miss/hit/partial-hit serving, cross-Encoder reuse, registration reuse,
byte-capacity chunking, explicit CPU staging under non-CPU default devices,
independent output storage, mixed batch results and over-capacity returns,
malformed-object isolation, mid-copy/event-record/completion failures,
shared-storage publication budgets,
consumed failure release, completed-publication reaping before the next load
(including empty inputs), and native I/O/shutdown ownership. The tests use their
own fixtures and omit the repository's global accelerator teardown.

71 affected proxy/shared-Store configuration and setup tests passed (27 proxy
and 44 shared-Store cases). Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy 3.10, passed.

Real Mooncake 0.3.12.post1 tests on H20 TCP passed 19 checks, including one
registration over interior slots, bounded chunk reuse, bit-exact FP16/BF16/FP32
GPU outputs, missing/short/oversized/malformed-object isolation and final buffer
unregistration. Full-object reads return actual short lengths; oversized reads
return `INVALID_PARAMS` (-600).

Seven alternating serial/batch resolver measurements per warm condition used
one or four objects of 16 KiB, 1 MiB and 30 MiB, with full hits, partial hits and
misses. Four-object full-hit p50 changed from 3.05 → 0.41 ms, 4.51 → 1.14 ms and
29.44 → 20.59 ms respectively. Four hits changed eight read calls/registrations
per request into one batch read with no registrations after initial allocation.
Full misses perform no reads or staging allocation. These small same-node
measurements cover lookup, I/O and completed copies, not serving throughput.

Serving validation with Qwen3.5-4B BF16, MRv2 and TP1 passed 45 assertions:
full hits skipped Encoder work, partial hits recomputed only the missing image,
and actual P2P-delivered tensors were bit-exact against cold computation.
All 32 generated token IDs matched. Full and partial hits each used one native
batch read and reused the same pinned staging buffer. The completed cold
request from job 3020 was preserved; job 3027 restored those exact tensors into
the Store and completed the serial/batch comparisons and partial-hit phase.
SLURM job 3027 completed with verified task process/port/GPU/IPC cleanup.

Three warm serving requests per implementation had Encoder-request medians of
21.62 ms (serial) and 18.21 ms (batch); approximate E→PD TTFT medians were
97.94 ms and 96.43 ms. The first batch request was slower (623.71 vs 596.08 ms
approximate E→PD TTFT). These are small supplementary samples; TTFT here sums
Encoder HTTP duration and PD time to first nonempty content.

GPU validation reused the `6e1d051fc` PR-base wheel with the candidate's 10
EC/config/shared Store Python modules, without a native rebuild. The tested
batch-read diff is unchanged after rebasing onto the independently published
consumed-traceback fix.
Follow-ups enforce each GET destination capacity, explicitly allocate staging
on CPU, and reap completed publications before the next Store resolution or
Encoder computation. The current 52 CPU cases and changed-file pre-commit
passed; duplicate tests were consolidated. GPU measurements above cover the
preceding batch-read implementation.

PUT header-only follow-up: on H20 / Mooncake 0.3.12.post1 / same-node TCP,
a no-eviction rerun with a 16 GiB Store used three alternating rounds
(30 warm samples per case/path). Median PUT processing time fell from 1.466 to
1.183 ms for 1 × 1 MiB and from 5.088 to 4.118 ms for 4 × 1 MiB (about 19%).
Small-object gains held across all three rounds. For 30 MiB objects the medians
were 15.678 to 15.378 ms (one object) and 61.846 to 61.600 ms (four objects);
the four-object result was noisy and does not establish a stable improvement.
All 780 PUT payloads and headers were verified outside timing. Each candidate
client registered its header once and unregistered it after draining; payload
registration was unchanged. Final Store usage was 11.81/16 GiB, with zero
eviction attempts and zero allocation failures. This supersedes the earlier
6 GiB run, which encountered eviction. These are asynchronous publication
processing measurements, not TTFT.

## Controlled performance result

### Setup and comparison

We evaluated InternVL3_5-38B-HF BF16 on six H20 GPUs on one node, using common
CPU single-tile preprocessing. Each measured request contained four images,
approximately 400 text tokens and 32 output tokens. All instances used TP1;
EPD delivery used Mooncake P2P over TCP.

| Configuration | Six-GPU deployment | Encoder output caching |
|---|---|---|
| M6 (non-EPD) | Six monolithic instances, each running Encoder, Prefill and Decode | Existing instance-local cache |
| EL (local-only EPD) | Two Encoders + four Prefill/Decode instances (2E4PD) | Existing Encoder-local cache |
| ES (shared-cache EPD) | Same 2E4PD topology as EL | Existing Encoder-local cache + shared RAM Store |

**EL → ES is the primary comparison:** topology, inputs, arrival times and
forced E/PD routes are identical; ES adds shared output reuse. M6 provides an
equal-GPU system reference, showing how the EPD configurations compare with
monolithic serving. M6 → EL/ES also changes resource partitioning and delivery,
so it does not isolate the cache's effect.

Each configuration replayed the same fixed, open-loop Poisson arrival trace
at nominal 2 requests/s: 128 measured requests and 512 distinct images. The
client did not wait for one response before sending the next request. All
128 requests completed successfully in each configuration.

### Reassignment workload

We use `seed → ownership swap → measurement`. During seeding, EL and ES process
the same images, and ES publishes the outputs to the shared Store. E0 and E1
then exchange image ownership so each target Encoder has a local-cache miss.
EL recomputes the embedding, while ES reuses the shared output and skips
Encoder execution. Each of the 512 images is measured once after reassignment
to avoid subsequent local-cache hits.

### Results

Encoder GPU time is cumulative CUDA-event time during measurement; it excludes
Store access and does not represent reclaimable whole-GPU time.

| Metric | M6 (non-EPD) | EL (local-only EPD) | ES (shared-cache EPD) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Completed requests | 128/128 | 128/128 | 128/128 |
| Re-encoded images | 512 | 512 | 0 |
| Encoder GPU time | 53.661 s | 55.484 s | 0 s |
| TTFT p50 | 1.173 s | 1.209 s | 0.819 s |
| TTFT p90 | 1.197 s | 1.656 s | 0.891 s |
| TPOT p50 | 19.17 ms | 19.33 ms | 19.33 ms |
| TPOT p90 | 54.53 ms | 41.54 ms | 41.39 ms |

Relative to EL, ES eliminates the 512 repeated Encoder executions and reduces
TTFT p50/p90 by **32.3%/46.2%**, with essentially unchanged TPOT. The E fan-out
completion span falls from 364.40/823.80 ms to 48.39/69.84 ms at p50/p90.
TTFT is measured from scheduled arrival to the first nonempty generated SSE;
client dispatch lag p90 was below 1.7 ms in all three configurations.

### Cold-miss publication overhead

During the closed-loop seeding phase, EL and ES compute the same 512 Encoder
outputs; ES additionally publishes 1.25 GiB of embeddings asynchronously.

| Seeding metric | EL | ES | Observed change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Wall-clock time | 129.71 s | 130.01 s | +0.23% |
| Encoder GPU time | 56.821 s | 57.131 s | +0.55% |
| Store data published | 0 | 1.25 GiB | — |

All 512 publications completed successfully, with no pending writes at phase
completion. Per-request cold-miss TTFT was not measured separately.

### Reduced Encoder work

The 2E4PD topology concentrates vision-encoder work on two E workers, while
M6 distributes it across six monolithic instances. Cross-Encoder reuse
eliminates repeated forwards and reduces demand on the Encoder tier,
shortening the embedding-preparation path in this experiment. This can ease
Encoder capacity pressure when reusable outputs are available.

**Scope.** These results use one run per configuration in a controlled 100%
Encoder-reassignment workload on one model over same-node TCP. They quantify
the benefit when cross-Encoder reuse opportunities exist; production reuse
frequency is not evaluated here.

**Cost.** Shared reuse requires additional Store RAM and I/O: ES writes
1.25 GiB during population and reads 1.25 GiB during reuse. Asynchronous
population showed a +0.23% aggregate wall-clock increase in this experiment.
The prototype performance experiment was not repeated after the final refactor.

## Related work and assistance

Related to the [EPD tracker #52409](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52409).

This builds on [Mooncake P2P #41567](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41567).
Store client operations were originally adapted from
[Store EC #47302](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47302). The current
v3 namespace uses its own 24-byte header for complete 2D embeddings.
#47302 focuses on Encoder → Prefill transfer through Mooncake Store, while this PR focuses on
cross-Encoder output reuse to avoid redundant Encoder computation. Store is
used as a shared computation cache here, while the existing
`ECMooncakeConnector` remains the E→P delivery path.

Overlapping Store helpers require coordination during upstream integration.

[Processor cache #53809](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53809) caches
multimodal preprocessing results. This PR caches Encoder outputs after model
execution and does not replace that preprocessing cache.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, and documentation.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Reduce CUDA graph divergences
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
This PR cuts down on some ROCm-specific divergences that have now outlived their use. This serves as a cleaner base for the ModelRunner V2 default enablement on ROCm (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56360).

1. Reverts https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48526, which performed graph capture profiling on the current stream rather than a new side stream on other platforms after a performance regression was observed. The reason given then was that a side-stream "shifts the KV/activation buffers' physical placement and slows every bandwidth-bound decode kernel ~20%"; this is not correct.
The true reason is due to a latent runtime defect involving long cross-stream waits which was subsequently fixed in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53712 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55099. In particular, the revert is now measured to be performance neutral rather than incurring a 20% slowdown.

2. Reverts #55095's DS V4 fallback on ROCm to `CudaGraphMode.NONE` if MRV2 is enabled. The justification given was #52644, but it no longer applied on `main`, so DS V4 was suffering an unnecessary performance degradation on ROCm with MRV2 enabled.

3. Gate `compile_or_warm_up_model`'s `torch.compile` specialization warmups not only on whether the compilation mode is `VLLM_COMPILE` but also on whether there's even a torch.compile'd submodule.

## Test Plan
Full `gsm8k` was run on DS V4 before/after these changes (2 in particular), on both ModelRunner V1 and V2, and accuracies between 0.954-0.972 were observed.
Performance was measured on TP8, concurrencies 1, 8, 32, 128, 256, 8K/1K, on DS V4 and Qwen-3.5-35B after these changes, and found to be the same (within noise).

Main and AMD CI will also be run on this PR. 

## Test Result
There are no new regressions in CI.

commits.pr_title: [A2A] Allow EPLB + SharedExpert Overlap + DeepEPv2
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Allow shared expert overlap when EPLB is enabled with the `deepep_v2` all2all backend, by adding `deepep_v2` to `_EPLB_OVERLAP_SAFE_BACKENDS`. This follows #50569, which made the same exemption for `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` after validating it.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR touches `_EPLB_OVERLAP_SAFE_BACKENDS` for `deepep_v2`. Sequence-parallel support for `deepep_v2` is a separate PR (#57210); it was applied locally only for the SP runs below. When SP is active, `_disable_shared_experts_overlap` returns early, so this change only affects TP=1 deployments.

## Test Plan

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`
- Hardware: 8×H200, single node
- Backend: `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`
- Execution: `--enforce-eager` (see note on CUDA graphs below)
- Environment: `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, because the node has no InfiniBand NICs. vLLM's `_check_gin_support` does not honor `EP_DISABLE_GIN`, so the GIN query was skipped locally (after the communicator-init probe). That change is not part of this PR.
- EPLB: async (the default), rebalancing aggressively so experts move many times during each eval:

```bash
EP_DISABLE_GIN=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-eplb --eplb-config '{"use_async": true, "window_size": 50, "step_interval": 100, "num_redundant_experts": 4}' \
  --all2all-backend deepep_v2 --enforce-eager \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 2048

python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --num-questions 1319
```

- SP runs: same command with `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2` and #57210 applied. The logs confirm `sp_size=2`.
- Baseline (overlap off): same command with this PR's one-line change reverted.

## Test Result

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot. Each accuracy is from a separate eval run against the same server.

| Config | EPLB | Shared expert overlap | GSM8K accuracy | Async rebalances |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 (**this PR**) | async | on | 0.353 / 0.353 / 0.346 | 52 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 (baseline, PR reverted) | async | off | 0.349 / 0.346 / 0.354 | 52 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4 | off | on | 0.352 | – |
| TP=2, DP=2, EP=4 (SP, #57210) | off | off (SP disables it) | 0.350 / 0.356 / 0.349 | 0 |
| TP=2, DP=2, EP=4 (SP, #57210) | async | off (SP disables it) | 0.357 / 0.351 / 0.359 | 51 |
| TP=1, DP=4, EP=4, `allgather_reducescatter` (reference) | off | – | 0.361 | – |

Enabling overlap with async EPLB on `deepep_v2` shows no accuracy change against the baseline, and there were no errors or hangs across 52 rebalances. SP combined with async EPLB on `deepep_v2` also works as expected.

**Known issue, unrelated to this PR:** with `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1` on this node, `deepep_v2` produces garbage output (GSM8K 0.000) whenever CUDA graphs are enabled. This happens with or without EPLB, and with the shared experts stream on or off. Eager mode is correct, so all results above use `--enforce-eager`. This will be tracked separately.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to run the validation and draft this description. I have reviewed the change and the results.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix Nixl+Offloading PD edge cases on TheRock image
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
This PR fixes two issues observed on the (MI300) MultiConnector (Nixl+Offloading) PD edge cases test group on TheRock image (observed [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13000/list?sid=01a0a804-5e41-45dc-81bc-82b154c38890&tab=output) and [here](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002/list?sid=01a0a870-9608-4b69-970f-f7eb2ea5138f&tab=output)).

1. There is plenty of spam of the form `ucp_worker.c:3328 UCX  DATA  arm iface 0x39efd290 returned Success`. Resolved by bumping the AINIC version up to match what's currently in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`, per the previous updates in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54112 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56459.

2. `test_prefill_cpu_offload_after_gpu_eviction` fails the direct output match test. This was root-caused to slight (reasonable) numerical differences in the prefix cache hot vs cold path. See for instance the following issues:
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33123
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/5543#issuecomment-4625222702
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54490
    - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42699

This is compounded by the particular eviction prompt here being an open-ended exposition with many plausible continuations. In particular, the next-token logprobs were measured:
- ROCm 10:  ' However' -2.2956 / ' In' -3.3581   → margin 0.0625
- ROCm 7.2:  exact tie above on a cold cache     → margin 0.0000

i.e. almost or exactly tied between the top 2 candidates. The two observed diverging CI continuations (' The development...' vs ' The field...') are exactly the tied top-2 candidates.
Prefix-caching hit in this case legitimately shifts logits by ~0.005–0.06. This is measured to be backend-independent (triton 0.06, AITER 0.074). A 0.0625 margin sits inside that noise floor, so a hot-vs-cold shift can flip the argmax and cause direct text-matching to fail.
Fix: For direct text-matching to be reliable here (insensitive to small reasonable numerical divergences), the continuation has to be reliable i.e. not invite open-ended drift. Appending a sentence to count to 5000 ensures this while still preserving the spirit of the test. In particular, the exact eviction prompt is irrelevant, and slight numerical differences between the prefix cache hot-vs-cold paths are not what is under test here.
 
## Test Plan
All NixlConnector tests were run [before](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13002) and [after](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13014) this PR on ROCm 10 and it was found to fix the failing test group and remove the UCX clutter while not causing any test regressions.

Main and AMD CI will also run on this PR on ROCm 7.2 to verify it causes no new regressions both on the AMD and Nvidia code paths.

## Test Result
All NixlConnector tests pass on ROCm 10 without clutter, and there are no new regressions on ROCm 7.2 and on CUDA.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Bump vllm-proto to 0.3.0
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Prepare a new `vllm-proto` release so downstream Rust consumers, including Dynamo, can use `ParallelismInfo.data_parallel_size_local` from #57116. The schema change is merged, but the crate version remains 0.2.0. Adding a generated public struct field can break Rust struct literals even though the protobuf change is wire-compatible, so this bumps the pre-1.0 minor version to 0.3.0.

Update the crate manifest, workspace lockfile, and README dependency example. After merge, a maintainer must push `proto-v0.3.0` on the merged commit to trigger the upstream crates.io publishing workflow; merging this PR alone does not publish.

Searched open PRs for `proto 0.3.0` and `57116 in:body`; no overlapping proto release-bump PR was found.

## Purpose

The EC (Encoder Cache) connector has no metrics infrastructure today: there
are no stats hooks on `ECConnectorBase`, no stats field on
`ECConnectorOutput`, and nothing in `SchedulerStats`/the CLI or Prometheus
loggers. The KV connector already solved this (`KVConnectorStats`, worker→scheduler aggregation, CLI + Prometheus logging, all gated behind connector-class hooks), so this PR ports that same plumbing to EC.

This is intentionally scoped to **base infrastructure only**: every new hook defaults to `None`/no-op, exactly like `KVConnectorBase`'s own defaults. 

Changes:
- `vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/metrics.py` (new): `ECConnectorStats`, `ECConnectorLogging`, `ECConnectorPromMetrics`, `ECConnectorProm` — mirrors `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/metrics.py` almost verbatim.
- `vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/base.py`: `get_ec_connector_stats()` instance hook (callable from either a worker-side or scheduler-side connector instance) and `build_ec_connector_stats()` / `build_prom_metrics()` classmethods.
- `vllm/v1/outputs.py`: `ECConnectorOutput.ec_connector_stats` field.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/ec_connector.py`: populates the field in `ActiveECConnector.maybe_get_output`'s `finally` block (MRv2 only)
- `vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/utils.py`: `ECOutputAggregator.aggregate()` now folds each worker's `ec_connector_stats` into the aggregated `ECConnectorOutput`,

- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: aggregates worker-reported and scheduler-side EC stats in `update_from_output`, threaded through `make_stats()` into `SchedulerStats`.
- `vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py`: `SchedulerStats.ec_connector_stats` field.
- `vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`: CLI (`ECConnectorLogging`) and Prometheus (`ECConnectorProm`) wiring, mirroring the KV side's `LoggingStatLogger` and `PrometheusStatLogger` integration exactly.


## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: [Core] Don't issue a blocking collective RPC during engine handshake
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`EngineCoreProc._make_ready_response()` calls `Executor.supports_draft_weight_updates()`,
which is a `collective_rpc` issued with **no timeout** (`v1/executor/abstract.py`). That
response is built inside `process_input_sockets()` **before** `ready_event.set()`, while
`EngineCoreProc.__init__` waits on the same event with a fixed timeout
(`v1/engine/core.py`):

```python
while not ready_event.wait(timeout=10):
    if not input_thread.is_alive():
        raise RuntimeError("Input socket thread died during startup")
    assert addresses.coordinator_input is not None
    logger.info("Waiting for READY message from DP Coordinator...")
```

A slow engine→worker round trip therefore stalls the handshake. With
`data_parallel_size=1`, `addresses.coordinator_input` is `None`, so the first expiry
raises a bare `AssertionError` and kills an engine whose workers are all alive and idle.
The front end then reports `Failed core proc(s): {}` — empty, because nothing actually
failed. At DP>1 the identical stall is benign: the loop logs and retries.

Observed on 8-GPU ROCm runs. The input thread's own traceback shows where it sits:

```
core.py     process_input_sockets      -> ready_response = self._make_ready_response()
core.py     _make_ready_response       -> self.model_executor.supports_draft_weight_updates()
abstract.py supports_draft_weight_updates -> self.collective_rpc(...)      # blocked, no deadline
```

**The round trip is avoidable.** `Worker.supports_draft_weight_updates()` short-circuits on
`self.weight_transfer_engine is not None`, and that engine is only ever constructed under
`if vllm_config.weight_transfer_config is not None` (`v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`). With no
weight-transfer config every worker returns `False`, so the RPC cannot change the answer.
This PR consults the executor only when weight transfer is configured. Behaviour with
weight transfer configured is unchanged.

Scope note: this removes the call that was observed blocking. It does **not** change the
`timeout=10` wait or the bare `assert`, which remain a trap for anything else that lands on
the pre-ready path. Those are worth addressing separately; the ordering of the DP-coordinator
subscription relative to the executor call makes that a larger change than it looks.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

The closest open PR is **#48871** ("Surface engine startup failure diagnostics where startup
actually waits"). It is **complementary, not overlapping**: #48871 changes
`v1/engine/core_client.py` and `v1/engine/utils.py` to improve *reporting* on the front-end
side, where startup waits. This PR changes `v1/engine/core.py` to remove the engine-side
*cause* of one class of those stalls. Neither subsumes the other, and with both applied a
stall that still occurs would be reported better by #48871.

Note both PRs add tests to `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py`, so whichever lands
second will need a trivial rebase there.

Also reviewed and distinct: #37757 (startup error logging UX), #51018 (DP world-group port
binding), #55137 (Mooncake bootstrap registration hang).

## Test Plan

Unit tests added to `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py`:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_client.py \
  -k "ready_response_skips_draft_rpc or ready_response_queries_executor" -q
```

- `test_ready_response_skips_draft_rpc_without_weight_transfer` — asserts the executor is
  **not** consulted and the reported value is `False`. Fails before this change.
- `test_ready_response_queries_executor_with_weight_transfer` — asserts the executor **is**
  consulted and its value is reported. Passes before and after, pinning the path this change
  must not alter.

End-to-end: Kimi-K3, TP8, MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10, `v0.29.1rc1.dev187`, with a probe
wrapping `Executor.supports_draft_weight_updates` and `_make_ready_response`.

## Test Result

Unit tests, run against the installed package in both an unpatched and a patched image:

| test | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `..._skips_draft_rpc_without_weight_transfer` | **FAILED** | passed |
| `..._queries_executor_with_weight_transfer` | passed | passed |

```
before:  1 failed, 1 passed
after:   2 passed
```

End-to-end on 8×MI355X, after the change:

```
[RPCPROBE] _make_ready_response built in 0.00s; supports_draft_weight_updates=False
[RPCPROBE] supports_draft_weight_updates() CALLED   ->  0 occurrences
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

commits.pr_title: [Scheduler] Add --max-num-active-seqs to cap RUNNING admission
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`max_num_seqs` currently does two jobs: it sizes the model runner (per-request buffers and CUDA graph capture) and it caps how many requests the scheduler will admit into RUNNING.

Those should be independent. Keeping runner/graph capacity large while admitting fewer decode requests lets a deployment hold a smaller decode batch without recapturing graphs or shrinking static buffers.

This adds an optional admission cap. Default `None` is current behavior (`max_num_seqs`).

This is not `--max-num-queued-reqs`. That limit is enforced in the API server across DP ranks and returns HTTP 503. This flag only gates WAITING → RUNNING inside one engine.

## Approach

- New `SchedulerConfig.max_num_active_seqs` / `--max-num-active-seqs`.
- Must be `<= max_num_seqs`. `None` uses `max_num_seqs`.
- The WAITING admission loop stops when `len(running) + streaming_slots >= max_num_active_seqs`.
- No preemption: lowering the cap takes effect as requests finish.
- Model runner, KV sizing, and cudagraph capture still follow `max_num_seqs`.

## Usage

```bash
vllm serve ... \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-active-seqs 16
```

## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: Use skip-redaction option for crcr-report
commits.pr_body:
## Depends on

https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra/pull/554

## Purpose

Make the nightly CRCR report actually post, now that
`small_cpu_queue_premerge` runs buildkite-agent 3.107.0 (ci-infra pin to
elastic-ci-stack v6.41.5).

Both `buildkite-agent` calls in the script need `--skip-redaction` to work
inside the container. The docker plugin mounts the agent binary and passes
`BUILDKITE_AGENT_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `BUILDKITE_JOB_ID`, but not
`BUILDKITE_AGENT_JOB_API_SOCKET` nor the socket, so anything that builds a Job
API client fails with `BUILDKITE_AGENT_JOB_API_SOCKET empty or undefined`.

- `secret get`: on 3.73.1 the secret was fetched and then discarded, because
  `jobapi.NewDefaultClient` was called unconditionally and `SkipRedaction` only
  checked afterwards — which is why the flag could not help before and why the
  step has skipped on every nightly since #54605. From v3.107.0 the client is
  built inside the guard, so the flag skips it.
- `oidc request-token`: OIDC tokens are auto-redacted via the Job API from
  agent v3.104.0. This call works today only because 3.73.1 predates that; the
  upgrade would start breaking it. Its `2>/dev/null` means the failure would
  surface only as `could not mint a Buildkite OIDC token -- skipping report`.

## Changes

`--skip-redaction` on both calls, plus a comment correcting the block at lines
53–59 which currently says the flag cannot help.

The flag must precede the key — urfave/cli v1 stops parsing flags at the first
positional argument.

Safe on both paths: the secret becomes a curl `Authorization` header, the OIDC
token is passed to `crcr_report.py` as an argument, neither is echoed, and the
script does not run under `set -x`.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: still gated on `TORCH_NIGHTLY=1` and
`main`, still best-effort, still `exit 0` on every failure path, still prefers
`BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN` from the environment.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Accept appended EngineCoreOutput fields
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With vLLM-Omni installed, its general plugin can append fields to Python's `EngineCoreOutput`. The Rust decoder rejects these longer arrays, breaking ordinary inference even when Python and Rust come from the same vLLM revision. This motivated the downstream workaround in https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/14731.

Keep the existing `Deserialize_tuple` derive and opt in at the output envelope with `#[serde_as(deserialize_as = "Vec<AllowTrailingFields>")]`. The shared adapter lets the generated decoder validate the known fields and apply defaults, then consumes unknown trailing values using `IgnoredAny`. It does not duplicate the schema or construct a dynamic tree for skipped values. No new dependencies are needed.

This matches [msgspec's append-only array-like schema evolution](https://msgspec.dev/schema-evolution) for ordinary vLLM output handling. It does **not** add full Omni serving support: Omni's frontend uses the extra fields for multimodal payloads, segment completion, and streaming prompt state. Serialization, standalone `EngineCoreOutput` deserialization, and other protocol structs retain their existing behavior.

Duplicate checks found no open PR addressing this trailing-field failure. Searches covered `msgpack`, `trailing fields`, `EngineCoreOutput Rust`, `Deserialize_tuple`, and `AllowTrailingFields`.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation and tests; the submitting author reviewed the change.


commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Ignore descales for unquantized AITER caches
commits.pr_body:
## Problem
`ROCM_AITER_FA` passes the attention layer's K/V scale tensors to AITER decode kernels even when the KV cache is unquantized. If those otherwise-unused tensors contain non-neutral values—for example, stale values left by dummy-weight initialization after loading real weights—AITER treats them as descales and corrupts attention output. In our MI300X reproduction, this reduced the post-reload InfoVQA score from the expected `0.952` to `0.000`.

## Solution
- pass null K/V descales to ROCm AITER decode kernels for unquantized KV caches
- preserve expanded descales for FP8 KV caches
- construct expanded descales only in unified-attention branches, avoiding unused eager tensor views in ordinary paged-attention decode
- add a ROCm backend correctness test with non-neutral scale tensors on an unquantized sliding-window cache

## Why this is not duplicate work
I searched open vLLM PRs for `AITER unquantized descale`, `ROCM_AITER_FA KV scale reload`, and `dummy weights attention scale` and found no PR addressing this behavior. [#53823](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53823) concerns prequantized FP8 attention and does not change descale handling for unquantized caches.

## Test plan
- [x] manual pre-commit hooks on the changed backend and test — passed, including Ruff and mypy for Python 3.10-3.13
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py::test_rocm_aiter_fa_unquantized_cache_ignores_kv_scales -v` on MI300X — 1 passed in 14.62s after the hot-path refactor
- [x] MI300X model evaluation with the equivalent backend change: InfoVQA reload score improved from `0.000` to `0.952` (4/4), with both CUDA graph recaptures succeeding

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Normalize native renderer reasoning controls
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Normalize reasoning behavior across the native Rust renderers for DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1, Harmony, Inkling, and Kimi K3.

### Behavior changes

1. **Apply deployment defaults.** Native renderers now consume reasoning controls from `default_chat_template_kwargs`, with request controls taking precedence over deployment controls and model defaults. An enabled request without a concrete effort can inherit deployment effort. Each source validates its selected input types before fallback.
2. **Unify control precedence.** `thinking` takes precedence over `enable_thinking`, and the top-level request effort takes precedence over kwargs effort. Explicit disabling discards effort; explicit enabling with `reasoning_effort="none"` inherits an enabled default effort. A standalone `"none"` disables reasoning.
3. **Align model input handling.** DeepSeek V3.2 recognizes standard effort as a thinking control; V4 and Harmony consume kwargs effort; V4.1 and Inkling follow the shared toggle/effort rules. K3 consumes standard `reasoning_effort` and ignores input `thinking_effort`. Model adapters retain their supported effort grades and ranges.
4. **Expose the resolved state downstream.** `effective_template_kwargs` now reflects the same mode and model-mapped effort used to build the prompt, including defaults. Both thinking aliases are synchronized; disabled reasoning exports `reasoning_effort="none"`. K3 also exports derived `thinking_effort` when enabled and removes it when disabled.
5. **Validate controls as request errors.** Selected thinking controls must be booleans, and active effort inputs must be strings or numbers; null effort means omitted. Invalid controls and unsupported model effort map to HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`, including cases previously classified as template errors.

HF template input handling is preserved.

Related work: #52739 covers Python effort remapping, #56708 covers Python DeepSeek flag precedence, and #54198 covers Python behavior documentation. This PR implements shared source resolution and prompt/kwargs consistency for Rust native renderers.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Enable AITER FP8/unquantized cases in modular-kernel sweep + fix MoRI per-tensor FP8 dispatch
commits.pr_body:
This is step 1 ("FP8/unquantized case identification") of the plan in #54966; the MXFP4 config/weight-conversion work needs gfx950 hardware and will follow separately.

### What

`AiterExperts` in the modular-kernel combinations sweep (`tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`) was only reachable indirectly through the general quant-config cross-product, with no assertion that the exercised `(weight_key, activation_key)` pair is one it actually declares supported. The harness also hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` everywhere, which on FNUZ FP8 platforms (gfx94x / MI300):

- unconditionally skipped this whole test file (`current_platform.is_fp8_fnuz()` module-level guard), so none of these cases had ever run on MI300/MI200-class hardware
- registered `AiterExperts` under `fp8_types` only, silently excluding the fully-unquantized `(None, None)` scheme it also supports

### Changes

- `mk_objects.py` / `common.py`: use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` / `is_fp8()` instead of the hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` literal (no-op on CUDA/gfx950, where `fp8_dtype()` returns the same literal); register `AiterExperts` under `common_float_types` (was `fp8_types`) so `(None, None)` is actually generated.
- `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: drop the module-level FNUZ skip; add `assert_aiter_quant_scheme_case()` to make the exercised `(weight_key, activation_key)` pair explicit and assert `AiterExperts._supports_quant_scheme()` agrees — gated on `fused_experts_type.__name__ == "AiterExperts"`, so no other backend is affected.

### Additional Fix: MoRI Missing Per-Tensor FP8 Dispatch

Broadening quant-config coverage also exposed a real bug (distinct from #57029): `MoriPrepareAndFinalize.prepare()` only quantized activations for block-quantized/per-token FP8, so per-tensor FP8 configs fell through to unquantized dispatch while weights stayed FP8, which surfaced downstream as a misleading `Unsupported rhs dtype fp8e4b8` Triton assertion.
Fixed in: (a.) `all2all_utils.py`: extend `use_fp8_dispatch`/`scale_dim` to `is_per_tensor` (b,) `mori.py`: add the per-tensor quant branch, broadcasting the scalar scale to `[num_tokens, 1]` since MoRI's dispatch reads scales via a raw pointer
Fixes: 
`test_modular_kernel_combinations_multigpu[... quant_config15-MoriPrepareAndFinalize-TritonExperts-2]`

### Pre-existing bug surfaced

Running on MI300 (gfx942) for the first time (previously skipped at module-level) reproduced a deterministic HIP `illegal memory access` for every `AiterExperts` × `{DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize, MoriPrepareAndFinalize}` combination at `world_size=2`, including the plain unquantized case. Filed as #57029 with a full repro; this PR adds a scoped skip referencing it so CI doesn't regress on this newly-exercised combination. Not fixed here.

### Test plan

On MI300 (gfx942, FNUZ FP8), 
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 pytest -sv tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py
```
All 6 target `(weight_key, activation_key)` pairs from #54966 (5 FP8 + `(None, None)`) verified individually, each triggering the new assertion. Confirmed the FNUZ-skip removal doesn't affect CUDA/gfx950, and that the DeepEP-HT/Mori skip actually suppresses the crash (ran that node id before/after).

### AI assistance disclosure

Portions of this change (diagnosis, harness edits, and the new AITER test infra) were developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). All changes were reviewed and the tests above were run and verified by me on MI300 hardware.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Metrics][MFU] Size activation traffic from the model dtype
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`BaseConfigParser` sizes weight traffic from the model's dtype but pins activation traffic to 2 bytes:

```python
args.weight_byte_size = get_dtype_size(torch_dtype)

# FIXME: handle this better by parsing whether activations use
# bf16, fp32, etc...
args.activation_byte_size = 2
```

`torch_dtype` is already resolved on the line above, so the two values come from the same config and disagree. For a model served with `--dtype float32`, every activation term in the MBU accounting is counted at half its real size while that same model's weight terms are correct. Activations are produced in the model's compute dtype, so this keys them on it.

`activation_byte_size` is set once here and never overridden. Quantization parsers override `weight_byte_size` (fp8, mxfp4 and friends) but leave activations alone, which is why the model dtype remains the right source after this change.

## Impact

- bfloat16 and float16: unchanged, 2 bytes, which covers the overwhelming majority of deployments.
- float32: 2 to 4 bytes. Activation read and write traffic doubles and reported MBU drops accordingly.

The float32 change is user visible. Anyone tracking MBU for a float32 deployment will see the number move; that movement is the correction, since the previous value understated memory traffic.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py
pre-commit run ruff-check ruff-format --files \
  vllm/v1/metrics/perf.py tests/v1/metrics/test_perf_metrics.py
```

New tests in the existing file:

- `test_base_config_parser_activation_byte_size_follows_dtype`, parametrized over float16, bfloat16 and float32, asserting activation and weight byte sizes agree with the dtype.
- `test_attention_read_bytes_scale_with_activation_dtype`, which goes through `AttentionMetrics.get_read_bytes_breakdown` and asserts `qkv_input`, a pure activation term, is exactly twice as large for float32 as for bfloat16.

The existing `test_base_config_parser` assertion of `activation_byte_size == 2` for float16 still holds and is unchanged; only its comment was updated, since 2 is now the dtype's size rather than a default.

## Test Result

```text
72 passed, 1 warning in 19.45s
```

That is the 68 pre-existing tests plus the 4 added here.

Linting:

```text
ruff check...............................................................Passed
ruff format..............................................................Passed
```

No model evaluation: this changes analytic MFU/MBU accounting only. No kernel, no model computation, and no output logits are affected.

## AI assistance

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix EAGLE and dense draft startup with EP
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

After #55914, pairing an EP-enabled MoE target with a dense EAGLE, EAGLE3, or independent draft model fails during configuration validation:

```text
Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled.
```

Pass the final draft `ModelConfig`, after draft architecture overrides, to `create_draft_parallel_config`. Disable inherited EP only when that config reports a dense draft through `ModelConfig.is_moe`, the same classification used by the existing validator. MoE drafts, including DeepSeek V4 MTP and DSpark, continue to inherit target EP. Target EP and target/draft TP settings remain unchanged.

The new `draft_model_config` argument is optional. Existing two-argument calls, or calls that explicitly pass `None`, retain the previous EP inheritance. The normal configuration-construction path always supplies the final draft config. This preserves helper-call compatibility; it does not infer draft density or fix existing validation failures for callers that omit model information.

## Test Plan

The regression constructs real `ModelConfig` and `SpeculativeConfig` objects from small local configuration files, exercising architecture conversion and production validation without mocks or model weights. Its 24 cases cover dense independent/EAGLE/EAGLE3 drafts and MoE independent/MTP/DSpark drafts, target EP on/off, and matching target/draft TP sizes of 1 and 2.

Four additional compatibility cases cover omitted and explicit-`None` draft model configs, each with target EP on/off.

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py tests/test_config.py
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k 'draft_inherits_ep_only_for_moe or draft_parallel_config_preserves_ep_without_model' -v
```

## Test Result

Rebased without conflicts onto public `main` at `fc8132a5e523294ea69decb5e7cbf50e9d3e135e` on 2026-09-16. The three existing patches are unchanged by the rebase.

- Pre-commit: passed.
- On the rebased head `a2e2e9035de0e81252cda7164198c4d2f5230a9d`: 28 passed.
- Before replacing the required boolean argument with the optional model config, all four new compatibility cases failed with `TypeError`.
- Negative control: keeping the optional helper and EP guard but omitting the draft config at the production call site caused 6 expert-count validation failures and 22 passes. The failures were dense independent/EAGLE/EAGLE3 drafts with target EP enabled. This confirms the configuration-level tests catch a missing call-site update even when the compatibility tests pass.
- On the earlier head `e679fb51c48b62b83920a24ea733bd4b3efb6cbe`, repeated the negative control using an in-process wrapper that deliberately omits the draft model config when calling the real helper: the same 6 dense-draft/target-EP cases failed with expert-count validation errors, and 22 passed. The on-disk source was unchanged.
- Full inference and model accuracy evaluations were not run; these tests cover configuration construction and validation only.

## Related work

This PR overlaps #56933, which addresses the same regression. Following review, this PR adopts the same backward-compatible optional-model-config interface, with an explicit legacy fallback and real configuration-construction regression coverage. These are alternative fixes, not dependencies; maintainers can select or consolidate the overlapping changes. #35143 addresses a separate dense-draft DP synchronization optimization.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Return prompt metadata from /inference/v1/generate
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Implement phase 2 of RFC #51472. Phase 1 (#51478) let `/inference/v1/generate`
resolve raw multimodal input (`content_parts`) internally. This phase exposes the
lightweight prompt metadata produced by that rendering path so token-in/token-out
RL callers can build loss masks, pack samples and carry the expanded history into
the next turn without re-rendering.

When `return_token_ids=true`, both the Python and Rust frontends now return:

- `prompt_token_ids`: the final prompt after multimodal placeholder expansion
  (same source as `chat/completions`' `return_token_ids`);
- `mm_placeholders`: ordered per-modality `{offset, length}` ranges into that
  prompt, the same shape `/render` returns in `features.mm_placeholders`.
  No pixel values or processed tensors.

Streaming responses carry both fields once, on the first emitted data chunk.
When the flag is omitted or false nothing is computed and the response shape is
unchanged.

### Design notes

- `mm_placeholders` is gated on the same `return_token_ids` flag: the ranges are
  offsets into `prompt_token_ids` and are meaningless without it, and reusing the
  existing flag keeps the request schema and the Python/Rust contract identical.
- The placeholder extraction that `/render` already does in
  `extract_mm_features()` is factored into `placeholder_ranges_from_engine_input()`
  so `/generate` and `/render` produce ranges from the same code without
  serializing `kwargs_data` (which would base64 the full `pixel_values`).
- Streaming parity: Rust already omits `None` fields on stream chunks
  (`skip_serializing_none`); Python now omits the two new keys when absent so both
  frontends emit the same JSON. Non-streaming responses emit `null` on both sides,
  matching the existing optional fields.
- A zero-token completion still emits its terminal chunk when metadata is
  pending, so `prompt_token_ids` is never lost; with the flag off that chunk is
  skipped exactly as before.
- Encoder-decoder models: `prompt_token_ids` is the decoder prompt (as in
  `chat/completions`); `mm_placeholders` is omitted because the offsets would not
  refer to that sequence.

### Why this is not a duplicate

#51478 added `content_parts` input but did not expose the resulting metadata.
#54659 added `features.mm_metadata` for E/P/D prefill and the
`extract_mm_features()` helper this PR reuses; it does not return metadata from
`/generate`. Searches for open PRs referencing #51472 and for
`prompt_token_ids` + `mm_placeholders` found no overlapping work.

## Test Plan

Python unit tests (`tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py`):
flag off/on for non-stream and stream, text-only prompt (no `mm_placeholders`),
multimodal prompt (ranges match engine input), encoder-decoder omits ranges,
`n=2` with an empty first output (metadata on the first emitted chunk only),
zero-token completion with flag on/off, absent keys omitted from stream chunks,
and `placeholder_ranges_from_engine_input()` directly.

Rust unit tests (`rust/src/server/src/routes/inference/generate.rs`): stream
default omits metadata, first emitted chunk carries it once (empty first output
skipped), late `prompt_info`, non-stream default omits, `extract_mm_placeholders`
on `None`/empty and multi-modality ordering.

Model-backed test (`test_serving_multimodal_tokens.py`, Qwen3-VL-2B): `/render`
→ collapse each placeholder range to one token → `/generate` with
`content_parts` + `return_token_ids` (non-stream and stream) → returned
`prompt_token_ids` and `mm_placeholders` must equal `/render`'s output. The
collapse step is required because `/generate` + `content_parts` expands
placeholders itself; sending `/render`'s already-expanded ids re-expands them
(RFC #51472 Problem 2, tracked separately).

## Test Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_mm_serde.py -q
# 50 passed

cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-server routes::inference::generate::tests --no-default-features
# 8 passed
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-server --tests --no-default-features -- -D warnings
# clean; cargo fmt --check clean

# only the three changed Python files bind-mounted over the installed package:

# 3 passed in 83s
```

`pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, rustfmt, SPDX, signoff) passes at commit time.

Model evaluation is not applicable: the change only exposes metadata the engine
already produces and does not alter generated tokens.

This PR was developed with AI assistance (OpenAI Codex for the initial draft,
Claude Code for the rebase, simplification and tests). An independent Codex

commits.pr_title: [BugFix][KV Connector] Fix Deadlock with KVConnector + MTP under KV Pressure
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Scheduler can deadlock under KV memory pressure with MTP + KV connector --- encountered in production deployment of GLM5.2

### Example

- 2 requests A (needs 4 blocks + 1 for mtp), B (needs 3 blocks + 1 for mtp)
- Total blocks 7

#### Step 1 — A and B arrive and get added to `skipped_waiting` queue

A is admitted (4 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`
B is admitted (3 blocks), popped from `waiting` -> `skipped_waiting`, `status → WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`

- result: 
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

#### Step 2 — A's transfer lands. 

Schedule the `skipped_waiting` queue first. Peek `skipped_waiting` → A.

`_is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS)` is True → `_try_promote_blocked_waiting_request(A)` succeeds → `A.status=WAITING` 

Then, schedule A. Need to allocate for the MTP blocks [these are only allocated after async load]. We need 1 block, but there is 0 left. `allocate_slots` returns None and we `break` (end attempting to schedule.

- result:
```
skipped_waiting = [A, B]
waiting = []

A.status = WAITING
B.status = WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV
```

As we can see, the queues are in the same state as before this step, and will continue to be in this state (trying to schedule A, asking to allocate blocks) forever.

#### Step 3 onward — Same cycle

Peek `skipped_waiting` → still A, now status WAITING. _is_blocked_waiting_status(WAITING) is False, so no promotion branch; straight to allocation; fails; break. Spin forever.

## Root Cause

Async KV load is allocated without lookahead slots (see `limit_lookahead_tokens`), and `_request_remaining_blocks()` -- which backs the `_inflight_prefill_reserved_blocks()` admission gate -- does not count them either. 

Then, after the `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KV` is done, we ask `allocate_slots()` for the lookahead margin on top ---> if this block is not available, we `break` --- with this request at the front of the `skipped_waiting` queue. If no requests are running, then no new blocks come free and we deadlock in this loop

**So there is a mismatch in the blocks reserved and what is actually needed to start running**

## Test Plan

- unit test
- reproducer (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57104#issuecomment-5701283900)

commits.pr_title: [Build] Bump DeepGEMM pin to a6bbb80
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Bump the `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` fork pin from `ad1f172` to `a6bbb800` (current head of the fork's `dev` branch), picking up three fixes:

- **[DeepGEMM#9](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/9)** — corrects the ported SM120 GEMM and MQA execution paths, and moves the SM120 regression tests into dedicated `tests/test_sm120_*.py` files so the fork's copies of upstream-owned test files stay byte-identical to `dev` (removes a recurring sync-conflict surface on upstream's per-release test rewrites).
- **[DeepGEMM#11](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/11)** — drops the Mega-Gate finite-score device trap. The selected-expert-ID clamp is retained; non-finite scores now propagate instead of aborting on device.
- **[DeepGEMM#13](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/13)** — raises `kNumTimeoutCycles` from 60s to 300s. That is the device-side spin-wait budget shared by *every* wait in `comm/barrier.cuh`: the NVLink cross-rank barrier, the intra-device grid sync, and the mega-MoE combine peer wait. At 60s it could fire on long-running multi-rank workloads that were still making progress, turning a slow peer into a device assert.

Both pin sites are updated: `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` and `tools/install_deepgemm.sh`, which each carry a comment requiring them to be kept in sync.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs against `vllm-project/vllm`:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "deepgemm"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "bump DeepGEMM"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open "install_deepgemm"
```

No open PR bumps the DeepGEMM pin. #56266 (`[DSv4.1] Integrate Mega-Gate from DeepGEMM`, draft) is the only open PR touching `deepgemm.cmake`, and it refactors the `FetchContent_Populate` block — it does not change `_DEEPGEMM_UPSTREAM_TAG`. No conflict beyond a trivial textual one if both land.

## Test Plan

The pin's risk is twofold: that the ref is fetchable as declared, and that DeepGEMM's `_C` still compiles against it. The changed `csrc/apis/{attention,einsum,gemm,sm120_dispatch}.hpp` are compiled into `_C` on every arch, so a `_C` build exercises them even on non-SM120 hardware.

1. Confirm the new ref is the `dev` head and fetches with the two submodules `deepgemm.cmake` declares (`third-party/cutlass`, `third-party/deep_jit`).
2. Build `_C` at the new pin using `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` — the same script `deepgemm.cmake` drives.
3. `pre-commit run` on the changed files.

## Test Result

```console
$ git ls-remote https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM.git dev
a6bbb8000161c0dc3a85a0300a905f76898a7913        refs/heads/dev

$ git submodule status
 f3fde58372d33e9a5650ba7b80fc48b3b49d40c8 third-party/cutlass (f3fde58)
 e5bdee2bc4ca519eba00cfc5f0c6e950e6a96a16 third-party/deep_jit (e5bdee2)

$ CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.1 .venv/bin/python tools/build_deepgemm_C.py <src> <out> .venv/bin/python
# succeeded; only pre-existing -Wattributes visibility warnings from deep_jit/utils/gil.hpp
$ ls <out>
_C.cpython-312-aarch64-linux-gnu.so
```

`pre-commit run` on the two changed files: all applicable hooks pass (`shellcheck`, `typos`, dockerfile-graph, spaces-in-filenames, config-validation); the rest are skipped as no-files-to-check.

Environment: GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.1, aarch64, Python 3.12.

## Evaluation

No model evaluation is included. This PR changes only a dependency pin and no vLLM code path. Of the three picked-up commits, none alters numerics on the hardware available here:

- #9 is SM120-only (this host is SM103), and its non-SM120 portion is a test-file reorganization inside DeepGEMM.
- #11 removes a device-side abort on non-finite Mega-Gate scores; it changes failure behavior, not values on well-formed inputs.
- #13 only lengthens a hang-detection timeout.

Evaluating the SM120 correctness fixes in #9 would need SM120 hardware, which I do not have. If a reviewer wants an eval on SM120 or a Mega-MoE accuracy run before merge, please say so and I will arrange it.

## Note on AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line, ran the commands above myself, and can defend the change end-to-end.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Bugfix] Initialize _transfer_layer_group_ids in region_pull_worker fixture
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

Main is red on `:computer: (CPU) V1 Others` (builds [#89375](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89375), [#89376](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89376)): all 7 parametrizations of `test_region_pull_ignores_allocation_padding` fail with

```
AttributeError: 'NixlPullConnectorWorker' object has no attribute '_transfer_layer_group_ids'
```

Root cause is a stale-base merge conflict between two PRs:

- **#50494** (merged Sep 15) added the `_transfer_layer_group_ids` attribute to the NIXL base worker and reads it in `base_worker.py:198` (`use_layer_name_routing = bool(self._transfer_layer_group_ids)`).
- **#57077** (merged Sep 16) added the `region_pull_worker` fixture, which constructs the worker via `object.__new__(NixlConnectorWorker)` and sets attributes manually — without `_transfer_layer_group_ids`. Its CI ran against a base that did not yet contain #50494, so the conflict only surfaced after both landed on main.

## Fix

Set `worker._transfer_layer_group_ids = ()` in the fixture — the same empty-tuple default the base-class `__init__` uses, and the same value the sibling `_make_mock_worker_for_desc_ids` fixture already sets.

Note: not runnable locally on my box (no torch), so validation is via CI — pre-commit hooks (ruff, mypy, DCO) pass.

Signed-off-by: kimi-no-na-wa <kimi-no-na-wa@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.pr_title: [Refactor] Remove unused interface methods
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`Parser` (`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`) was declared as the union of the legacy `ReasoningParser` and `ToolParser` interfaces plus `parse` / `parse_delta`. Only part of that is ever reached through the `Parser` type. The serving layer calls `parse`, `parse_delta`, `is_reasoning_end` (the prompt check), `count_reasoning_tokens` and `adjust_request`, and reads the `reasoning_parser` / `tool_parser` getters and the `*_cls` class attributes. The rest existed so `DelegatingParser` could compose its two legacy parsers, and `ParserEngine` inherited it even though its own `parse()` never goes through `extract_reasoning`.

This PR trims the base class to the members that are actually consumed through it.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Remove MegaMoE padding and shared padding workaround
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Remove unnecessary MegaMoE intermediate-width padding for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and revert the production workaround added in #56568. Routed and shared experts both retain the checkpoint width of 2304, so native shared-expert fusion remains enabled without padding either to 2560.

The bundled DeepGEMM uses `layout::Data(..., false)` for activation-scale rows in `include/deep_gemm/layout/mega_moe.cuh`; the old 16-byte TMA-row alignment rationale no longer applies. The existing runtime check still requires intermediate dimensions divisible by 128.

This removes 10% of the intermediate dimension used by the padded expert GEMMs and avoids the separate padded shared-weight copies introduced by #56568. Fusion keeps its existing eligibility checks and disable flag. A bare revert of #56568 would leave routed padding in place and disable V4.1 shared fusion again, so this change removes both together.

Retain the useful regression coverage from #56568, now checking exact checkpoint-shaped weight/scale preservation, native-width shared fusion, buffer reuse, and repeated finalization.

Related: #56217. Duplicate checks covered its issue/comments, open PRs mentioning #56217/#56568, and MegaMoE/shared-expert/padding searches. #56568 is already merged; this replaces its padding workaround. #54049 targets FlashInfer CuteDSL, #55275 adds GLM adapters, #40833 integrates a general fused-MoE backend, and #56697 targets SM90 Marlin. None removes this native DeepGEMM model-path padding.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/model.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py --hook-stage manual
```

Also compare this implementation directly with upstream `42919b49c5` on four GB200 GPUs using identical random expert weights, inputs, routes, and routing weights: hidden size 5120, intermediate width 2304 versus 2560, 384 experts, top-6, token counts 1/8/32/128/1024/2048, shared fusion both disabled and enabled. For the reference, upstream itself pads the native checkpoint-shaped shared weights.

## Test Result

Focused suite: **30 passed** on GB200.
Four-GPU operator comparison against upstream `42919b49c5`: **48/48 comparisons have exactly zero output error**, including all shared-fusion cases. Shared-expert outputs have nonzero contribution. Candidate commit: `21cda373e8`.
Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy 3.10, and explicit mypy 3.12 passed.

Previously completed real-weight model evaluation used this exact production model file with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/EP4. Full GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.12, five-shot multi-turn chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, 1024 output tokens, seed 123:

| Configuration | Correct / 1319 | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Auto-MoE/FlashMLA FP8-indexer baseline, three runs | 1270–1274 | 96.2851–96.5883% |
| Native-width MegaMoE/FlashMLA FP8 indexer | 1271 | 96.3609% |
| Combined optimized configuration, MXFP4 sparse indexer | 1266 | 95.9818% |

These are prior model-path validation results, not a newly measured isolated comparison against current upstream with #56568. The combined configuration includes separate attention/indexer optimizations. No new end-to-end speedup over #56568 is claimed here.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, validation, and this description. Woosuk Kwon authorized submission after the prepared diff and validation results were presented for review.

## Summary

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Expose local DP size in gRPC Control metadata
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Dynamo's in-process vLLM integration already supports [hybrid load balancing](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/serving/data_parallel_deployment/#hybrid-load-balancing). We are bringing the same multi-node DP topology to Dynamo's native gRPC sidecar integration, with a frontend and sidecar on each node.

Control currently reports global DP size and the first attached rank, but not how many ranks that frontend serves. For example, global size 8 and starting rank 4 do not tell the sidecar whether that frontend owns ranks 4–5 or 4–7. The sidecar needs the local count to register its rank range and normalize aggregate KV capacity.

Add `uint32 ParallelismInfo.data_parallel_size_local = 7`, populated from `EngineCoreClient::engine_count()`. This is the number of engines registered with the frontend after startup has waited for the configured engine set. Global DP size and starting rank remain unchanged. Zero means the local size was not reported, including responses from older servers; successfully started frontends always report a positive count. Consumers must treat zero as unknown rather than an empty rank range. Dynamo's legacy complete-group fallback is only valid at starting rank zero; nonzero-start ownership without a local count must be rejected.

Companion changes implement the downstream functionality:
- [Dynamo #14697](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/14697): consume local ownership in sidecar registration, KV capacity, and KV-event source validation.
- [srt-slurm #420](https://github.com/NVIDIA/srt-slurm/pull/420): launch the per-node native frontend/sidecar topology.

Searched open vLLM PRs for gRPC local parallelism and `data_parallel_size_local`; no overlapping change was found.

## Test Plan

- From `rust/`: `cargo test --locked -p vllm-server grpc::tests::control_`
- From the repository root: `pre-commit run --files rust/proto/control.proto rust/src/server/src/grpc/control.rs rust/src/server/src/grpc/tests.rs`

## Test Result

- All 6 Control tests passed. Coverage checks local count 1 for a single engine and local count 2 for complete and partial groups, including global DP8 with starting ranks 0 and 4. Aggregate KV capacity remains local to the attached engines.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- The equivalent schema/producer change was used with the companion Dynamo and launcher changes in a completed seven-node, 28-GB300 benchmark using global DP8/DP12 and local DP4. That run used a patched nightly build, not this exact upstream commit.
- No model accuracy evaluation: this change only exposes discovery metadata.
